gaps.sentence: He passed all his exams first time, ___ surprised everyone.
gaps.hint: refers to the whole previous clause
gaps.explanation: 'Which' can refer to a whole idea ('he passed first time'); this non-defining use never takes 'that'.

gaps.sentence: It was the best meal ___ I have ever eaten.
gaps.hint: after a superlative, this pronoun is preferred
gaps.explanation: After superlatives ('the best ...'), 'that' is the preferred relative pronoun in defining clauses.

gaps.sentence: Have you got anything ___ will remove this stain?
gaps.explanation: After 'anything', 'that' is the preferred relative pronoun; 'which' is avoided after -thing words.

gaps.sentence: The festival, during ___ the town is full of visitors, takes place in July.
gaps.hint: preposition + event in a non-defining clause
gaps.explanation: 'During which' is the formal pattern; 'during when' does not exist.

gaps.sentence: Nobody knows the reason ___ he resigned so suddenly.
gaps.explanation: 'The reason why ...' is the standard pattern; 'why' means 'for which'.

gaps.sentence: The bridge, on ___ repairs are still continuing, will reopen in May.
gaps.explanation: 'On which' is the formal pattern; 'where' cannot follow a preposition, and 'that' is barred from non-defining clauses.

gaps.sentence: The assistant ___ I spoke to was extremely helpful.
gaps.explanation: 'Whom' is the formal object form after a preposition-style clause.

gaps.sentence: The contract, the small print of ___ nobody had read, contained a surprise clause.
gaps.explanation: After a preposition only 'which' (things) or 'whom' (people) is possible.
